# PR: One share hub at bloom — image-first, and the link always travels (backlog 005)

**Risk tier (builder's guess): HIGH** — per the task's own pre-classification, 005.md's own
risk tier, and NORTH_STAR.md's risk map ("anything user-facing beyond copy/styling" → HIGH →
full explainer + quiz before merge). This removes an existing share surface, adds a new
primary action to the surviving one, and changes what leaves the user's device on the image
path. Git is unavailable in this environment, so this file is the PR: no branch, no commit
exists — everything below is working-tree edits reviewable at the paths cited.

## Goal
NORTH_STAR's north-star metric is `share_link_opened → plan_created` weekly closures, currently
zero because `share_link_created` itself is zero. Spec 004 tried surfacing the share CTA higher
in the page; a human production review the same day (2026-07-10) found two problems 004 didn't
fix: (1) TWO share surfaces render simultaneously in bloom — the new prompt card AND the old
footer row — which is confusing, not motivating; (2) of the three share mechanisms, the one the
human explicitly called out as the hero artifact ("users get an image with their garden
status — that could be even more viral") is the ONE mechanism that structurally cannot close
the loop, because a downloaded PNG carries no URL back to the site. Goal of this item: collapse
to one surface, and make the image mechanism carry the link too, so every share method can in
principle produce a `share_link_opened`.

## Intuition
`renderShareImage` already did the hard part (drawing a shareable 1200×630 card client-side on
canvas) — it just threw the plan away at the end and downloaded a plain image. The fix isn't a
new share mechanism; `doCopyLink` and `doNativeShare` already compute a shareable URL via
`encodePlanToUrl` and already report it to analytics correctly. The fix is plumbing: give
`renderShareImage` the same URL those two functions already have, and teach its *completion*
step (not its drawing step) to do something smarter with it than an unconditional download —
share the file+link together where the platform supports it (`navigator.canShare({files})`),
otherwise fall back to the existing download plus a clipboard copy of the link, mirroring the
copy-link button's own established fallback pattern.

The non-obvious part: doing this changes what "counts" as a share for the new method. Copy-link
and native-share fire their analytics event optimistically, at click time, before knowing if the
clipboard write or the OS share sheet actually completes — that's the existing, shipped,
already-endorsed behavior (NORTH_STAR: "share pipeline code-audited sound end-to-end"), and I
left it untouched. But the task's own instructions are explicit that the *new* `'image'` method
should fire "when the image path completes with the URL attached" — a deliberately stricter,
gated condition. I kept that asymmetry rather than "harmonizing" it away, because harmonizing it
would mean counting cancelled/failed image shares as successes in a metric whose entire purpose
is seeding a funnel that a doomed row can never satisfy.

## What changed, walking the diff in reading order

### 1. `translations.js` — one new string, both languages, at the very end of each `planner` block
```js
// en.planner, immediately after the existing waitlistStepLabel (was the last key):
shareImageSaved: "Image saved — link copied!"

// ko.planner, same position:
shareImageSaved: "이미지 저장됨 — 링크 복사됨!"
```
Placed at the literal end of each `planner: {...}` object (translations.js:476 / :938, right
before each object's closing brace) per the acceptance criterion's anchor rule, not adjacent to
the other `// Share` clusters mid-file — this avoids colliding with any other agent appending
translations the same day. No other new strings: every button label reuses existing keys
(`share`, `sharePrepping`, `shareLink`, `shareLinkCopied`, `shareNative`).

### 2. `planner.js` — new state (Bloom component, share-state block)
```js
// planner.js:1482-1486, right after the existing isSharing/copySuccess declarations
var imageShareConfirmState = useState(false);
var imageShareConfirm = imageShareConfirmState[0], setImageShareConfirm = imageShareConfirmState[1];
```
Drives a button-label toggle, the same idiom `copySuccess` already established — no new UI
element, no new CSS.

### 3. `planner.js` — `doShare` now computes and forwards the plan URL (planner.js:1686-1764)
All archetype-specific headline/subline branch logic (subscription/target/growth) is untouched.
Only the tail changed:
```js
var shareUrl = encodePlanToUrl(goal, monthly, years, persona, props.capital, props.fundingMode, props.deadline);
renderShareImage({
  headline: shareHeadline, goalLabel: goalLabel(t, goal), subline: shareSubline,
  footer: t('shareFooter'), years: slideYears, you: slideMonthly, apy: apy,
  drawChart: shareDrawChart,
  url: shareUrl,            // new
  shareText: shareHeadline  // new — the "one short line of text" the spec asks for
}).then(function (result) {
  setSharing(false);
  if (result && result.linkAttached) {
    if (typeof Analytics !== 'undefined') {
      Analytics.trackShareLinkCreated({ method: 'image', goal: goal, persona: persona });
    }
    if (result.method === 'download') {
      setImageShareConfirm(true);
      setTimeout(function () { setImageShareConfirm(false); }, 2500);
    }
  }
}).catch(function () { setSharing(false); });
```
`shareUrl` uses the identical call signature `doCopyLink`/`doNativeShare` already use — same
inputs, same helper, zero new URL logic. `shareText` reuses the already-computed headline
(the same line printed on the image itself), not a newly minted string.

### 4. `planner.js` — `renderShareImage`'s completion path extended, drawing code untouched
Everything through the canvas drawing (gradient, card, optional growth chart, headline
fit/wrap, subline, wordmark, footer — planner.js:2764-2891) is byte-for-byte unchanged. Only
the `c.toBlob(...)` callback (planner.js:2893-2960) was extended:
```js
function downloadImage() { /* the original 5 lines, unchanged, now a named closure */ }

if (!opts.url) {                       // doWaitlistDownload's call site — behavior preserved exactly
  downloadImage(); resolve(); return;
}

var shareFile = null, canShareFiles = false;
try {
  shareFile = new File([blob], 'my-defi-garden.png', { type: 'image/png' });
  canShareFiles = !!(navigator.share && typeof navigator.canShare === 'function' &&
    navigator.canShare({ files: [shareFile] }));
} catch (fileErr) { canShareFiles = false; }

if (canShareFiles) {
  try {
    navigator.share({ files: [shareFile], url: opts.url, title: 'My DeFi Garden',
      text: opts.shareText || opts.headline || '' })
      .then(function () { resolve({ linkAttached: true, method: 'native' }); })
      .catch(function () { resolve({ linkAttached: false, method: 'native' }); });
  } catch (shareErr) { resolve({ linkAttached: false, method: 'native' }); }  // sync-throw guard
  return;
}

downloadImage();                        // fallback: image via download,
try {                                    // link via clipboard (mirrors doCopyLink's own
  navigator.clipboard.writeText(opts.url) // writeText -> textarea/execCommand fallback shape)
    .then(function () { resolve({ linkAttached: true, method: 'download' }); })
    .catch(function () { /* textarea + execCommand('copy') fallback, same as doCopyLink */ });
} catch (copyErr) { resolve({ linkAttached: false, method: 'download' }); }
```
`doWaitlistDownload` (the waitlist panel's card-download button — explicitly out of scope per
005.md) never sets `opts.url`, so it always takes the first branch and is unaffected.

### 5. `planner.js` — `sharePromptElement` gets a primary button (planner.js:2560-2580)
```js
var sharePromptElement = e('div', { className: 'gp-share-prompt gp-animate-in' },
  e('p', { className: 'gp-share-prompt-text' }, t('sharePromptHeadline')),
  e('button', { type: 'button', className: 'gp-share-btn gp-share-prompt-btn',
      onClick: doShare, disabled: isSharing },
    isSharing ? t('sharePrepping')
      : (imageShareConfirm ? ('✓ ' + t('shareImageSaved')) : ('📸 ' + t('share')))
  ),
  navigator.share                      // secondary button — 100% unchanged from spec 004
    ? e('button', { ...onClick: doNativeShare }, '↗ ' + t('shareNative'))
    : e('button', { ...onClick: doCopyLink }, copySuccess ? '✓ Copied!' : '🔗 Copy link')
);
```
No new CSS needed: `.gp-share-prompt` (planner-styles.css) is already
`display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:var(--space-12)` and `.gp-share-prompt-btn` is
already `width:100%` unconditionally (both from spec 004) — the second full-width button just
stacks below the first.

### 6. `planner.js` — `footElement` loses its share row (planner.js:2347-2359)
```js
var footElement = e('div', { className: 'gp-bloom-foot gp-animate-in' },
  e('p', { className: 'gp-disclaimer' }, t('disclaimer')),
  e('p', { className: 'gp-press-mention' }, t('pressFeatureLabel') + ' ', e('a', {...}, t('pressFeatureName')))
);
```
The `.gp-share-row` div (3 buttons: image/copy/native) is gone. `gp-disclaimer` and
`gp-press-mention` ("As featured on Leviathan News") are untouched, per spec.

### 7. `planner-styles.css` — dead rules removed, one comment corrected
`.gp-share-row` and `.gp-share-link` (planner-styles.css, was ~1403-1413) deleted — confirmed
via repo-wide grep that nothing else referenced them (they existed solely for the footer row
just removed). `.gp-share-prompt`'s doc-comment updated to say it's now the only surface, not
an additive one; no rule bodies changed there.

## Deviations from spec
- **Asymmetric analytics gating** (detailed above): `'image'` fires only when
  `result.linkAttached` is true; `'copy'`/`'native'` still fire unconditionally at click time,
  unchanged. This is the literal instruction ("fire ... when the image path completes with the
  URL attached ... plus existing 'copy'/'native' paths unchanged"), not a reinterpretation.
- **No confirmation UI for a successful native file-share** — only the no-file-support fallback
  path shows "Image saved — link copied." A completed OS share sheet is its own confirmation;
  `doNativeShare` has never shown one either, so this matches existing product behavior rather
  than inventing a new pattern for just one path.
- **Added a try/catch around `navigator.share(...)` in the new native-file-share branch** that
  wasn't strictly named in the spec, because without it a synchronous throw from that call would
  leave the primary share button permanently disabled (see 005-notes.md, "Robustness fix"). This
  is a correctness fix for code this PR introduces, not scope creep into pre-existing code —
  `doNativeShare` itself is untouched.
- **Deleted `.gp-share-row`/`.gp-share-link` CSS**, not just the JSX. Confirmed orphaned
  repo-wide before deleting; this is the direct cleanup of what was removed, not a drive-by
  refactor of unrelated styles.
- Everything else (URL/router semantics, `analytics.js`, waitlist/checkout panel, the share
  image's visual design, referral/attribution params) — untouched, as OUT of scope in 005.md.

## Verification performed
`cd defi-garden-neumorphic && node test_planner.js && node test_protocol_parsing.js && node
test_qualifier_fix.js` — all three exit 0, verified individually (not just via `&&` short-
circuiting): test_planner.js 190/190 assertions, zero failures; the other two scripts complete
with their expected output, no errors. Re-ran after every edit, including after the post-
self-review robustness fix; last run clean. `node -c planner.js` / `node -c translations.js`
syntax-clean; `require('./translations.js')` loads and both new `shareImageSaved` keys resolve
correctly. Brace-balance sanity check on `planner-styles.css` (567/567). Grep-verified: exactly
one `onClick` wiring each for `doShare`/`doCopyLink`/`doNativeShare` (all inside
`sharePromptElement` — no orphan handlers); zero remaining references to `gp-share-row`/
`gp-share-link` anywhere in the repo; `footElement`/`sharePromptElement` still present in both
bloom return branches (subscription; target/growth).

No new test file was written — this change adds no new pure/testable helper (matches spec 004's
precedent); it's React markup plus browser-only APIs (`canvas`, `Blob`, `File`,
`navigator.share`, `navigator.clipboard`) the plain-Node harness can't exercise. **Not
independently browser/screenshot-verified** — no browser tool was available in this
environment; see the final summary for exactly what a human should eyeball on production.
